summary: Stephen Hislop (1817–1863) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the University of Glasgow (~1834–1837), earned an M.A. from the University of Edinburgh (~1837–1840), and studied under Thomas Chalmers (~1840–1843).

Stephen J. Laumakis is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Notre Dame (1985–1991) and studied under John Kronen, Ramdas Lamb, George J. Tanabe, and David West, later joining the University of St. Thomas in 1990.

Stephen Jenkins is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Harvard University under doctoral supervisors Masatoshi Nagatomi and Charles Hallisey, alongside several other teachers, and served as Professor of Religious Studies at California State Polytechnic University, Humboldt (attested 2010–2013).

Stephen Meredyth Edwardes (1873–1927) was an Indologist and historian. He studied at Eton College (~1887–1891) and Christ Church (~1891–1894), later serving as secretary of the Indo-British Association (~1919–1927) and editor of the Indian Antiquary (1923).
Stephen Montagu Burrows (1856–1935) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at Eton College (~1870–1875) and Exeter College, Oxford, where he earned a B.A. (~1875–1879).

Stephen N. Hay (1925–2001) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology, earning a B.A. from Swarthmore and an M.A. and Ph.D. from Harvard. He held posts at the University of Chicago (1956–1964), Harvard (1964–1966), and UC Santa Barbara (1966–1991).

Stephen Prothero (born 1960) is a religious studies scholar who earned a B.A. from Yale and an M.A. and Ph.D. from Harvard, where he studied under William R. Hutchison. He was appointed at Boston University starting around 1996.

Stephen R. Bokenkamp (born 1949) is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who studied at UC Berkeley (~1978–1986). He taught at Indiana University Bloomington (~1989–2007) before becoming Professor of Chinese at Arizona State University (~2007).
Stephen Suen is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2009) under the supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti.

Stephen Wootton Bushell (1844–1908) was a Sinologist and historian who earned an MD from the University of London. After medical posts at Guy's Hospital and Bethlem Royal Hospital, he served as physician to the British Embassy in Beijing (1868–1900).

Steve Odin (born 1953) is a philosophy and Japanology scholar. He studied at Stony Brook University (~1975–1980) under David A. Dilworth and Edward S. Casey, and became a Professor of Philosophy at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa in 1982.

Steven Collins (1950–2018) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. Educated at Oxford under Richard Gombrich, he held posts at Bristol (~1980–1987), Indiana University (~1987–1991), and the University of Chicago as Chester D. Tripp Professor starting in 1991.

Steven Edward Lindquist is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Texas at Austin (ending 2005) under Patrick Olivelle, studied under several traditional teachers, and held a post at Concordia University.

Steven Heine (born 1950) is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He earned his Ph.D. at Temple University, studied under Shudo Ishii, and held posts at Villanova, La Salle, Penn State, and Florida International University (since 1997).

Steven Lukes (born 1941) is a philosopher and sociologist who studied at Oxford under E. E. Evans-Pritchard. He held professorships at Balliol College, Oxford (1966–1987), Florence, Siena, the European University Institute, LSE, and New York University (~2002–2021).

Steven Neal Weinberger is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Amherst and the University of Virginia (Ph.D. 2003 under Jeffrey Hopkins), he trained under numerous traditional teachers and held a post at the University of Virginia (attested 2006).

Steven Vose is an Indology, religious studies, and history scholar. He completed degrees at St. Lawrence, Harvard, and Penn (Ph.D. 2013), and held posts at Florida International University (2013–2021), Colorado College, and the University of Colorado Denver (2022).
Stewart McFarlane is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology who held posts in the Department of Religious Studies at Lancaster University (attested 1991, 2001).

Sthaneshwar Timalsina (born 1965) specializes in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Martin Luther University, later teaching at Nepal Sanskrit University, San Diego State University (~2005–2018), and Stony Brook University (~2018).
Sthira Bhattacharya is an Indology and history scholar. Bhattacharya studied at the University of Chicago (Ph.D. 2019–2026) and was appointed there as a Postdoctoral Teaching Fellow in 2026.
